blocks.text: Being immersed, one should enter with one’s own mind.
blocks.directed: Being immersed, one should enter with one’s own mind.

blocks.text: Use Your Mind to Enter the State Beyond Your Mind. Brilliant. Thanks.
blocks.directed: Use Your Mind to Enter the State Beyond Your Mind. Brilliant. Thanks.

blocks.text: We’ve been instructed to infuse it into waking, dreaming and deep sleep.
blocks.directed: We’ve been instructed to infuse it into waking, dreaming and deep sleep.

blocks.text: And now Vasugupta tells us to enter with our own mind.
blocks.directed: And now Vasugupta tells us to enter with our own mind.

blocks.text: Wasn’t the mind the instrument of limitation?
blocks.directed: Wasn’t the mind the instrument of limitation?
[short pause] Didn’t Book III literally begin:

blocks.text: And now we’re supposed to use the mind to transcend the limitations of mind?
blocks.directed: And now we’re supposed to use the mind to transcend the limitations of mind?

blocks.text: Cittena — with the mind or consciousness, instrumental singular.
blocks.directed: Cittena — with the mind or consciousness, instrumental singular.

blocks.text: Praviśet — one should enter, from pra-viś, to enter into.
blocks.directed: Praviśet — one should enter, from pra-viś, to enter into.

blocks.text: Now, Kṣemarāja explains that the practitioner must enter through an inwardly directed, nonconceptual awareness.
blocks.directed: Now, Kṣemarāja explains that the practitioner must enter through an inwardly directed, nonconceptual awareness.

blocks.text: He specifically discusses relinquishing reliance on the grosser procedures of practice.
blocks.directed: He specifically discusses relinquishing reliance on the grosser procedures of practice.

blocks.text: The deliberate operations employed in earlier stages.
blocks.directed: The deliberate operations employed in earlier stages.

blocks.text: Because once the practitioner has approached the conscious source through these methods, the final entry isn’t accomplished simply by multiplying techniques.
blocks.directed: Because once the practitioner has approached the conscious source through these methods, the final entry isn’t accomplished simply by multiplying techniques.

blocks.text: Imagine using a ladder to climb onto a roof.
blocks.directed: Imagine using a ladder to climb onto a roof.

blocks.text: But when you’ve reached the roof, you don’t continue climbing the ladder indefinitely.
blocks.directed: But when you’ve reached the roof, you don’t continue climbing the ladder indefinitely.

blocks.text: At some point you have to step off.
blocks.directed: At some point you have to step off.

blocks.text: Otherwise you’re going to end up standing on the top rung, clutching the ladder, asking whether there’s a more advanced ladder available.
blocks.directed: Otherwise you’re going to end up standing on the top rung, clutching the ladder, asking whether there’s a more advanced ladder available.

blocks.text: This is the situation Kṣemarāja is describing.
blocks.directed: This is the situation Kṣemarāja is describing.

blocks.text: The methods prepare and orient the practitioner.
blocks.directed: The methods prepare and orient the practitioner.

blocks.text: But the recognition of consciousness itself cannot be reduced to another mechanical operation.
blocks.directed: But the recognition of consciousness itself cannot be reduced to another mechanical operation.

blocks.text: Now, he quotes the Netratantra concerning the movement beyond gross and subtle forms of prāṇāyāma towards the supreme spanda.
blocks.directed: Now, he quotes the Netratantra concerning the movement beyond gross and subtle forms of prāṇāyāma towards the supreme spanda.

blocks.text: Because spanda doesn’t simply mean ordinary physical vibration.
blocks.directed: Because spanda doesn’t simply mean ordinary physical vibration.

blocks.text: Nor is it merely the sensation of energy moving around the body.
blocks.directed: Nor is it merely the sensation of energy moving around the body.

blocks.text: It’s a technical term associated with the dynamic, self-revealing nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: It’s a technical term associated with the dynamic, self-revealing nature of consciousness.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja places this supreme reality beyond the gross and subtle movements of vital energy.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja places this supreme reality beyond the gross and subtle movements of vital energy.

blocks.text: So even the highly refined experiences associated with breath are not the ultimate goal.
blocks.directed: So even the highly refined experiences associated with breath are not the ultimate goal.

blocks.text: The practitioner moves beyond identification with them.
blocks.directed: The practitioner moves beyond identification with them.

blocks.text: Then, through inward awareness, enters the supreme condition.
blocks.directed: Then, through inward awareness, enters the supreme condition.

blocks.text: And here he uses the term avikalpaka.
blocks.directed: And here he uses the term avikalpaka.

blocks.text: But awareness no longer structured around the ordinary conceptual divisions of subject and object.
blocks.directed: But awareness no longer structured around the ordinary conceptual divisions of subject and object.

blocks.text: And now comes the really beautiful phrase.
blocks.directed: And now comes the really beautiful phrase.

blocks.text: The astonishing delight of inward reflexive awareness.
blocks.directed: The astonishing delight of inward reflexive awareness.

blocks.text: The extraordinary delight in that recognition.
blocks.directed: The extraordinary delight in that recognition.

blocks.text: Now the practitioner is entering the conscious reality underlying the entire performance.
blocks.directed: Now the practitioner is entering the conscious reality underlying the entire performance.

blocks.text: Not by finding one more object to observe.
blocks.directed: Not by finding one more object to observe.

blocks.text: But by releasing the identification that made the body, breath and mental faculties seem to constitute the ultimate experiencer.
blocks.directed: But by releasing the identification that made the body, breath and mental faculties seem to constitute the ultimate experiencer.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja explicitly describes the dissolution of the notion that the body and vital energy are the true knowing subject.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja explicitly describes the dissolution of the notion that the body and vital energy are the true knowing subject.

blocks.text: He cites the Svacchandatantra and Vijñānabhairava, as well as a hymn attributed to Pradyumnabhaṭṭa, in support of this inward transformation. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He cites the Svacchandatantra and Vijñānabhairava, as well as a hymn attributed to Pradyumnabhaṭṭa, in support of this inward transformation. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now think about the apparent paradox.
blocks.directed: Now think about the apparent paradox.

blocks.text: The mind is used to direct attention.
blocks.directed: The mind is used to direct attention.

blocks.text: But what is ultimately recognised is not merely another mental object.
blocks.directed: But what is ultimately recognised is not merely another mental object.

blocks.text: It’s the consciousness through which the mind itself appears.
blocks.directed: It’s the consciousness through which the mind itself appears.

blocks.text: You can examine the structure of an experience.
blocks.directed: You can examine the structure of an experience.

blocks.text: But eventually the investigation points towards the very reality making the investigation possible.
blocks.directed: But eventually the investigation points towards the very reality making the investigation possible.

blocks.text: And the relation between observer and observed changes.
blocks.directed: And the relation between observer and observed changes.

blocks.text: The mind has become a vehicle of recognition.
blocks.directed: The mind has become a vehicle of recognition.

blocks.text: But by becoming transparent to its own conscious source.
blocks.directed: But by becoming transparent to its own conscious source.

blocks.text: And there’s something rather funny about this.
blocks.directed: And there’s something rather funny about this.

blocks.text: You’ve spent thirty or forty sūtras trying to discover the Self.
blocks.directed: You’ve spent thirty or forty sūtras trying to discover the Self.

blocks.text: And now Vasugupta is essentially telling you:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And now Vasugupta is essentially telling you:

blocks.text: “Right. Now stop clinging to all the machinery.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Right. Now stop clinging to all the machinery.”

blocks.text: “But I spent YEARS learning the machinery.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “But I spent YEARS learning the machinery.”

blocks.text: The intellect can help orient recognition.
blocks.directed: The intellect can help orient recognition.

blocks.text: But it cannot substitute for recognition itself.
blocks.directed: But it cannot substitute for recognition itself.

blocks.text: Now, apparently, we’re going swimming again.
blocks.directed: Now, apparently, we’re going swimming again.
